 04 High Home says the printer “Sends files over Wi-Fi” right after the connection failed 
 Back on Home, the Creality K1 card carries the line “Sends files over Wi-Fi”. The connection test had just failed. The line appears because the address was saved to the printer profile regardless of the test result, and the Home backend reads only whether an address exists. 
 The K1 card after the failed test, before c922876c66. The card menu: “Connect…” is the right escape hatch, but the card above it contradicts it. Kenneth's wireframe for the redesigned card (2026-09-24): header with dot and job, then Connection, Model and Loaded rows, then the action. 
 Why it matters. This is a false claim in the one place the user will look to check the printer's state. The next thing they do is slice and press Print, and it fails again, now far from the conversation that could help. 
 Suggested change. The host half is fixed: since c922876c66 the address and key are saved only when the test passes, so this exact screen no longer occurs. The rest is a redesign of the card, settled in the comment thread and side chats on 2026-09-24, so that every line on it rests on something the app has verified. The card has a header and three fact rows, in a fixed order, and a row with nothing to say is left out rather than filled with a placeholder. Header: the printer's name; at the right, a dot and, while a job runs, “Printing · 43%” with the progress bar under the header. The dot finally means one thing: green for Online and Connected, the warning colour for Offline, no dot for Not connected, with a visually hidden label carrying the same word. Connection row , one vocabulary for both kinds of printer: Bambu says Online (data in the last 30 s), Offline (verified before, silent now, with Reconnect), or Not connected; Moonraker and OctoPrint say “Connected · 192.168.1.42” once an address is saved, or Not connected. “Sends files over Wi-Fi” and “Can't reach it” go. Two gaps accepted: a host set up through Orca's own settings dialog reads Connected on a typed address, and a healthy Bambu printer reads Offline during the 30-second window after the app switches presets or the person signs out. Model row: “X1 Carbon · 0.4 mm”, the model from the preset with the vendor stripped, the nozzle from the preset or, when connected, the device's own reading. Loaded row , in three steps: material names with colour swatches when both are known (a connected Bambu printer's AMS trays, or spools the person described with a colour); material names as text with no swatches when only the material is known; no row at all when nothing is known. Home reads only the spool store today; a connected Bambu printer's trays come through the same discovery the setup chat already uses. The material label stops coming from the project's filament preset, which is a project fact, not a printer fact. Action: one button per printer kind, not per state. “Launch monitor” on a Bambu card opens Orca's native device panel as today. “Open printer page” on a Moonraker or OctoPrint card opens Orca's existing web-view Device tab on the printer's own page (Mainsail, Fluidd, OctoPrint); today the card never offers it because its gate is “has device data”, which only Bambu satisfies. Opening it may switch the project's selected printer preset, which is Orca's own Device-tab behaviour and is why the label says what it opens. Not in this change: live job status for Moonraker printers (the agent exists in Orca with its status stream compiled out behind an #if 0 , and switching it on is separate work), any OctoPrint status agent, and Spoolman. The implementation handoff is printer-card-redesign-handoff.md in the repository root, untracked.

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.

guard, then the user immediately found two things I never tried: the Agent chat panel

- Run the screen's primary gesture end to end in the app before calling UI work done,

- Config levers that remove blockers without clicking: `default_page=1` lands on the

name: windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop
description: How to drive real JusPrin UI gestures on the Windows box when the RDP session is disconnected (SetCursorPos and screen capture both die; send WM_ messages and read geometry instead)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c818cfcf-07b0-4d84-a4d6-a69c1bd9fdde
  modified: 2026-09-09T22:06:52.556Z
---

When the RDP session to the Windows verification box is **disconnected** (`query session` shows state `Disc` for the `guitest` session), `SetCursorPos`/`mouse_event` silently do nothing — `GetCursorPos` keeps returning 0,0 — and `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` throws "The handle is invalid". Only a *connected* session has an input desktop.

**Why:** This looks exactly like an application bug — gestures appear to have no effect and screenshots fail — so it can burn a long time before you realise the session, not the code, is the problem.

**How to apply:**
- Check `query session` first when input or capture stops working.
- Real UI testing still works without a desktop: `SendMessageTimeout` WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_MOUSEMOVE / WM_LBUTTONUP / WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK straight to the child HWND. This goes through the real wxMSW window procedure, real `SetCapture`, and real double-click handling — strictly more real than the harness's `ProcessEvent` injection, which bypasses `MSWWindowProc` entirely.
- A faithful drag must hold the pointer at a fixed **screen** x and recompute the client x from the target window's live `GetWindowRect` each step. Holding client x fixed makes a moving splitter run away, because the app converts with `ClientToScreen` against the window's current position.
- Read results from `EnumChildWindows` + `GetWindowRect` rather than pixels; assert that sibling columns tile the client rect exactly, which catches overlaps a per-window size check cannot see.
- P/Invoke `GetWindowTextW` must be declared `CharSet=CharSet.Unicode`, or the StringBuilder is marshalled as ANSI and the W call overruns the buffer and crashes PowerShell.
- The harness holds `shell_integration_harness.exe` open; kill it before relinking or the link fails with LNK1104.
- See [[windows-build-machine]] for the Mesa/GL and toolchain facts.

**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` and
`colour` are optional and cosmetic for that same read.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

I've implemented the handoff: steps 5.1 to 5.5. In the real app, right after a failed connection test, Home now says **Not connected** where it used to say "Sends files over Wi-Fi". Nothing is committed yet: the repo's `entire` commit hook hangs on this machine, so I need you to decide how to commit.

**The problem, as I understood it:** the card's connection line only checked whether an address was saved, not whether the connection worked. c922876c66 already stopped saving an address when the test fails. This change rebuilds the card so every line rests on something the app has actually checked. It follows your wireframe and the section-2 decisions.

**What changed**
- **Backend** ([OrcaHomeBackend.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp)):
  - Bambu printers say Online · LAN, Online · Cloud, Offline (with Reconnect) or Not connected. Moonraker/OctoPrint printers say Connected · address or Not connected. The address is shown without its scheme or any saved password.
  - A Model row, e.g. "X1 Carbon · 0.4 mm".
  - The Loaded row reads a connected Bambu printer's trays; otherwise it uses the spools the person described.
  - "Open printer page" selects that printer and opens Orca's Device tab on its web page.
- **Page** ([PrinterCard.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx)): every card has the same shape. The dot shows only the connection, with a hidden label for screen readers. Rows with nothing to say are left out. One button label per printer kind.

**Where I departed from the handoff**
- **Job line:** "Printing · 43% · 2h left" sits on its own line under the name. At the rail's 320 px width it pushed the name completely off the header.
- **Model names:** they come from the vendor profiles already in memory. Loading the printer catalogue instead cost 434 ms on the GUI thread at the first Home render. The catalogue's brand-splitting is now a shared function rather than a copy.
- **Two input bugs fixed:**
  - Discovery drew a white swatch for a tray that reported no colour.
  - The fake printer sent the filament type in a form upstream ignores, so its spools never had a material.
- **Where the wording is tested:** in the shell harness against the real backend, not in `test_home_host`, which uses a fake backend.
- **Branch:** this worktree was on `main`, so I moved its empty branch to `jusprin-newui`, which the handoff targets.

**Verification**
- HomeUI Vitest: 59 tests pass, including a new `PrinterCard.test.tsx`. The styles test also passes.
- Unit tests all pass: `jusprin_tests` 52 cases, `agent_bridge_tests` 254, fake-printer tests 10.
- Shell harness `--printer-setup` passes all 163 checks, 0 failures. 17 checks are new:
  - The finding-04 moment itself.
  - The host card and "Open printer page": the Device tab loads the saved address.
  - A fake Bambu printer reads Not connected before verification, Online · LAN after, and Offline once it goes silent. Its trays show "PLA #5F7D4F" and a PETG spool with no swatch.
  - To make those checks run, I also fixed a hang in the harness's stand-in print host: the web view's extra connections blocked it from shutting down.
- Screenshots of every card state, light and dark, are the two images I sent. They come from the built page under a scripted host, not from the running app.

**Not verified or still open**
- **Default harness mode fails on plain `jusprin-newui` as well** (two baseline runs). It stops at check 140 on "missing enabled header menu item: Filament settings…". It depends on timing, so it isn't caused by this change. I flagged it as a separate task.
- **Not tested:** "Open printer page" with unsaved changes in the project (handoff risk 7), and a host printer that is switched off.

**Your decision:** `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg` hangs even when run on its own, so every `git commit` stalls. `--no-verify` wouldn't skip that hook. Can you commit from your side, or fix the hook and tell me? I planned three commits:
1. Tray colour and fake-printer fixes.
2. The card redesign (5.1–5.4).
3. "Open printer page" (5.5).

input.prompt:
Investigate how filaments and spools should be handled in JusPrin, and write a proposal: current behaviour, the problems, options, and a recommendation. Don't implement until the direction is agreed.

What prompted it (2026-09-25, live-testing the Home printer-card redesign on branch claude/printer-card-messaging-906fb4):
- Home's printer cards have a "Loaded" row (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx, filled in `OrcaHomeBackend::printers()` in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp). For a connected Bambu printer it lists the AMS trays the device reports, via `PrinterSetup::discover_printers()` spools. Otherwise it lists `Workspace::SpoolStore::spools_for(printer_name)`.
- In a fresh data dir, three printers were added and never given spools by the person. Each card still showed a "PLA" spool in teal, the project's current filament colour; the header chip read "Teal PLA". The shell records a spool automatically when a printer is selected: see the "seed" code in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp, around lines 340 and 435 (`seed.colour = colour`, `spool.colour = colour`). The card redesign's rule is that every line rests on something verified. An auto-recorded project filament shown as "Loaded" on a printer breaks that rule.

Map the whole picture:
- `Workspace::SpoolStore` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SpoolStore.hpp): what a spool is, and who writes to the store and when. That includes StatusRow seeding, the spool chip and menu (Shell/SpoolMenu.cpp), the printer setup conversation (`OrcaPrinterBackend::change_printer` with spools), rename and remove of printers, and connected-printer trays.
- How Orca's own filament presets and per-extruder colours in the project relate to spools. Also the Bambu AMS trays (DevFilaSystem), and what the setup chat tells the model about spools (AgentUI printerInstructions.ts).
- What each surface shows: the header spool chip, the spool menu, Home cards, the printer panel, and the Agent context.

Questions to answer:
1. Should the app record spools on its own (seeding), or only when the person says so or a printer reports them? If it seeds, how is a seeded spool marked, and should Home show it?
2. One source of truth per printer: device trays versus remembered spools versus project filament. What should win when they disagree, and what shows when a Bambu printer goes offline?
3. Spools without a colour, or without a material: how are they stored and shown?
4. The relationship to future Spoolman support. The Home card handoff lists Spoolman as out of scope.

Deliver the proposal in the final message. Include the data flow as it is now, the specific code locations, options with trade-offs, a recommendation, and how you would verify it. The shell harness can build Home cards through the real backend: `home_card()` in tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp.

input.tldr: In live testing, Home's printer cards only refreshed when entering Home. A printer that started printing or went offline kept its old card until you left and came back. input.prompt:
Investigate and propose how Home's printer cards should update live while Home is on screen; implement once the approach is clear and cheap.

Found 2026-09-25 while live-testing the Home printer-card redesign on branch claude/printer-card-messaging-906fb4 (base it on that branch or on jusprin-newui once that work is merged):
- Home's page is fed by `HomeHost::push_state` via `HomeWebView::refresh()` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/HomeWebView.cpp). Today `refresh()` is called only when entering Home (`ShellController::on_page_changed`, src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp around line 550) and from printer-panel callbacks (around lines 250-254). Nothing refreshes on device events. So a Bambu printer that starts printing, changes progress, goes Offline (the 30-second freshness window, `PrinterSetup::has_recent_printer_data`), or reports new AMS trays keeps its old card until the person leaves Home and comes back. The same applies to print-host changes and to spool-store changes.
- The rail is built by `OrcaHomeBackend::printers()` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp). It calls `discover_printers()` once per build; a build costs about 36 µs on the test box.

Please:
1. Find the upstream events that fire when device state changes (DeviceManager or MachineObject updates, push_status parsing, `EVT_UPDATE_MACHINE`-style events, the Monitor's timers, etc.). Also find how other fork surfaces keep current: the header's status row and spool chip (Shell/StatusRow.cpp) and the printer panel.
2. Decide what should trigger a Home refresh:
   - device updates, throttled;
   - the Offline transition, which happens by time passing rather than by a message, so it needs a timer;
   - print-host and profile changes;
   - spool-store changes (`store_changed`).
3. Keep it cheap and quiet. Refresh only while Home is visible, coalesce bursts, and send nothing when the snapshot hasn't changed; consider comparing the serialized state payload. Don't let a refresh disturb the page: an open card menu, a rename dialog, scroll position, or the highlight animation.
4. Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must follow agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md. Prefer binding to existing events from fork code.
5. Verification: the shell harness drives a fake Bambu printer through `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json`. See src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md; states include idle, printing with progress, and offline. `home_card()` in tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp reads cards through the real backend. Add a harness check that the Home page's pushed state (not just the backend) changes from Online to Printing to Offline without leaving Home. See memory notes windows-build-machine and verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app for Windows-box specifics.

Report the chosen triggers, their cost, and the verification results in the final message.

Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-25, Entire CLI 0.11.0): when the committing session has file changes to link,
`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and reads the
answer from `CONIN$`, not stdin. The agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so the open succeeds and the read blocks forever.
`</dev/null` does not help. Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt, which is why it looked intermittent.
The log is buffered, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows nothing until the process exits.
Evidence: handle dump of the hung process showed a `\Device\ConDrv` handle with a blocked synchronous read.
Entire's own Pi integration prefixes agent bash commands with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for this exact reason.
With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` the same hook finished in ~0.3s and added the trailer, 3 of 3 runs; without it, 3 of 3 hung.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.
A separate, real slowdown also exists: an `msbuild -m` build pins all 16 cores (processor queue ~64) and every
`entire` launch then takes 5-20s. That is slow, not hung; don't confuse the two.

**How to apply:** Fixed 2026-09-25: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set as a user env var (HKCU\Environment), so Claude and Codex
shells inherit it after the app restarts (verified in Claude: 3/3 hook runs 0.3s with trailer). If a commit hangs again, first check
`echo $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in the agent shell. Restarting the Claude app: the tray has no Quit, so end all `claude` processes
from a helper launched via WMI (outside Claude's tree) and relaunch with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`.
If one hangs anyway, kill only that commit's `entire` PID; never `--no-verify`. See [[windows-build-machine]].
